document.claim_ceiling: An idealized, counter-propagating pair can have increasing local E_cm as r approaches r_s, but this is neither attainable outgoing flow from an ordinary Schwarzschild horizon nor a measured/escaping boom. Two identical infallers have finite E_cm=2mc^2.
limitations: Only radial e=1 geodesics and Schwarzschild; ignores spin, backreaction, finite size, scattering cross sections, quantum fields and emission transport.
The static local frame ceases to exist at the horizon; r=r_s is not sampled and no infinite-energy collision is claimed.
E_cm is local invariant center-of-mass energy; multiplying by sqrt(f) is an algebraic check, not a general escape-energy law for collision products.
Outgoing geodesic's white-hole provenance makes the head-on benchmark non-realistic for an ordinary astrophysical collapsing Schwarzschild black hole.

model.collision: Equal-mass radial geodesics at one event, e1=e2=1 (rest at infinity)

model.worldline_warning: Outgoing e=1 geodesic near an eternal Schwarzschild horizon implies a white-hole-origin trajectory. Not an ordinary collapsing black-hole outflow.
